land.text: Yingqiu, where Duke Tai was enfeoffed; the page does not locate it

predecessors.note: 'Qi was founded shortly after the Zhou conquest of Shang, c. 1046 BCE'; infobox 'Enfeoffment of Duke Tai: 1046 BCE'. A Zhou fief (vassal tint until 751 in the zhou-dynasty dossier).

land.text: Qi, 'the last to fall' of the Warring States, conquered by Qin in 221

successors.note: Infobox 'Conquered by Qin: 221 BCE'; the history text says 222. Cliopatria keeps a Qi shape to 219.

land.text: the revived Qi of 206-204, 'Defeated by Liu Bang'

successors.note: The Eighteen Kingdoms page: 'Tian Du, Qi: western and central Shandong | Defeated by Liu Bang'; Han Xin's conquest of Qi is not on the page (page silent); Cliopatria ends this Qi in 204.

capitals.name: Yingqiu
capitals.note: Infobox 'Yingqiu (11 c.–866 BCE)'; 'Enfeoffed by King Wu of Zhou, with capital at Yingqiu'. The page does not locate Yingqiu or Bogu; the coordinates are those of Linzi, a placeholder at the researcher's reading.

capitals.name: Bogu
capitals.note: Infobox 'Bogu (866–859 BCE)'; Duke Hu 'moved capital to Bogu'. Location not on the page; Linzi's coordinates used as a placeholder.

capitals.name: Linzi
capitals.note: Infobox 'Linzi (859–221 BCE)'; Duke Xian (859?-851) 'moved capital back to Linzi'. Linzi was 'invaded and sacked in 284 BC by General Yue Yi of Yan' (King Min page); the king fled to Ju. The revived Qi of 206-204 is assumed to sit at Linzi (page silent).

rulers.name: Duke Tai (Jiang Ziya)
rulers.title: Duke
rulers.note: Lead: 'Jiang Ziya (Lord Tai; r. 1046–1015 BCE)'. The next five dukes (Ding, Yi, Gui, Ai, Hu) have centuries but no years on the page and are omitted.

rulers.name: Duke Kang (Dai)
rulers.title: Duke
rulers.note: 'Deposed by Duke Tai of Tian Qi, died in 379'; Tian He held the power from 404.

rulers.name: Duke Tai of Tian (Tian He)
rulers.title: Duke
rulers.note: 'Recognized as Qi ruler in 386 BCE'; the page's reign is 404-384. House of Tian replaces the house of Jiang.

rulers.name: King Wei (Tian Yinqi)
rulers.title: King
rulers.note: 'Most powerful Qi ruler of the Warring States'.

rulers.name: King Min (Tian Di)
rulers.title: King
rulers.note: Page 300-283; 'Temporarily declared himself "Emperor of the East"'; Linzi sacked in 284, he fled to Ju.

rulers.name: King Xiang (Tian Fazhang)
rulers.title: King
rulers.note: Restored after the Yan occupation (279, Warring States period page).

correction.text: Duke Tai's fief at Yingqiu, 'enfeoffed by King Wu of Zhou'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the fief before Cliopatria's first shape (-750): Duke Tai's Qi from 1046 (infobox 'Enfeoffment of Duke Tai: 1046 BCE') with the capital at Yingqiu. The page gives no extent and does not locate Yingqiu; the 60 km disc round Zibo (Linzi) is the researcher's reading, confidence 1 on the place; a vassal tint of the Zhou until 751.

102,632 km2 for 750-551, 115.4-122.7 E, 35.8-38.7 N: the whole Shandong peninsula. The states table of the Spring and Autumn period page has Qi annexing Zhu (祝) 768, Tan (譚) 684, Ji 690, Sui 681, Guo 670, Zhang 664, Yang 660 and Lai 567 ('Annexed the State of Lai', Duke Ling), none located by any page, so the peninsula east of Lai may be early; the shape stands, unverified: no page places Lai. The Qi page has no area figure.
86,900 km2 for 550-481: Cliopatria hands 84 cells in the west (115.5-116.9 E, 36.0-38.3 N) to Jin; no page opened dates or names that land (ledger confidence 1). Otherwise the same outline as 750.

86,900 km2 for 480-405, the same outline as 550. 'In 532 BCE, the Tian clan destroyed several rival families'; Tian Heng killed Duke Jian in 481 (Qi page and the Spring and Autumn period footnote). No territorial change.

119,883 km2 for 404-351 (+33,000 km2 against 405): the shape reaches 115.6 E and 34.8 N, taking Lu's eastern half (128 cells), Zhu (29), a strip of Jin's Hebei edge (29) and 2 of Xu. The Spring and Autumn period states table has Xue and Pi 'to Qi' 418 and Cheng 'to Qi' 408; the Warring States page '(Lu was occupied by Qi)'; the Yue page 'invaded Qi and Lu' in 404. The Qi page has no area to compare.
119,901 km2 for 350-292: 2 cells more than 404 (page silent). Unchanged in substance.
119,867 km2 for 291-285. The conquest of Song in 286 ('Song | 286 BCE | to Qi') falls inside this shape's years but Cliopatria adds the Song land only in 284; the ledger carries 286.

correction.text: Qi without the Song land that it 'lost' after 286

keyframe_review.note: 129,744 km2 for 284-248, 114.5-122.7 E, 34.7-38.7 N, which contains the Song land (113 cells, 76 of them Song's). The King Min page says Qi 'was promptly attacked in its turn and lost all the territory it had gained' after 286, and Linzi fell in 284 with 'all but two cities of Qi' conquered, so Song's land cannot stay in Qi's shape to 248. Cliopatria hands it to Chu in 247 (106 cells); the shape is corrected to remove the cells that Chu holds in 247. The Yan occupation (284-279) is a ledger occupation, not a shape. The Qi page has no area.
109,290 km2 for 247-224: Qi after the Song land goes to Chu in Cliopatria. This is the outline the corrected 284 shape also takes; 'Qi never regained its power' (King Min page).
109,365 km2, the single year 223; 1 cell more than 247 (page silent).

correction.text: Qi as drawn, for -222 only; Qin's from 221

keyframe_review.note: 109,211 km2 for 222-219. Qin conquered Qi in 221 on the infobox ('Conquered by Qin: 221 BCE'; the history text says 222 and 'which was the last to fall'), so the shape is right for 222 only; from 221 to 219 the land is Qin's (the qin dossier adds a 221 keyframe). Years change, the shape does not.

60,204 km2 for 206-204, 115.3-119.6 E, 34.7-36.9 N, western and southern Shandong. The Eighteen Kingdoms table: 'Tian Du, Qi: western and central Shandong'; the rest of the old Qi (eastern and northern Shandong) went to Jiaodong (Tian Fu) and Jibei (Tian An), 'collectively known as the Three Qis'. The page gives no area.

ledger.note: c. 1046: King Wu enfeoffs Duke Tai (Jiang Ziya) at Yingqiu. 'Qi was founded shortly after the Zhou conquest of Shang, c. 1046 BCE'; infobox 'Enfeoffment of Duke Tai: 1046 BCE'; rulers table 'Enfeoffed by King Wu of Zhou, with capital at Yingqiu'. The page does not locate Yingqiu.
866: the capital moves from Yingqiu to Bogu. Infobox 'Yingqiu (11 c.–866 BCE) Bogu (866–859 BCE)'; Duke Hu 'moved capital to Bogu; killed by Duke Xian'.
859: Duke Xian moves the capital to Linzi. Infobox 'Linzi (859–221 BCE)'; Duke Xian (859?-851) 'moved capital back to Linzi'.
550: Cliopatria hands 84 cells of Qi's west (about 17,000 km2) to Jin. Page silent on the Qi, Spring and Autumn period and Warring States pages; the year is the shape's.

418: Xue and Pi pass to Qi. The states table: 'Xue, Pi | 418 BCE | to Qi' (the Chu dossier has Pi to Chu 'After 418'). The table does not locate them; the cells are the part of Zhu's shape that Qi holds from 404, a reading. Cliopatria shows the land in Qi's shape in 404.

region.text: Lu's east and south (116.9-120.6 E, 34.8-36.5 N), about 26,000 km2

ledger.note: 404: Qi holds the eastern half of Lu's old shape. The Warring States page: '(Lu was occupied by Qi)', undated; the states table has Cheng 'to Qi' 408 and Xue and Pi 418; the Yue page: Yue and Jin 'invaded Qi and Lu' in 404. The year is Cliopatria's, confidence 1. The matching loss is in the lu dossier.

region.text: 29 cells of Jin's old edge (115.6-116.7 E, 36.3-37.1 N)

ledger.note: 404: 29 cells of Jin's old shape pass to Qi in Cliopatria. Page silent.

386: the house of Tian replaces the house of Jiang. 'In 386, the house of Tian fully replaced the house of Jiang as rulers of Qi'; rulers table: Duke Tai of Tian 'Officially recognized as Qi ruler in 386 BCE'. Earlier: Tian clan 'destroyed several rival families' in 532; Tian Heng killed Duke Jian in 481. Same state, same colour.

286: Qi destroys and annexes Song. The states table: 'Song | 286 BCE | to Qi'; the King Min page: 'In 286 BC, King Min attacked and destroyed Song'; the Song page: 'the kingdom was finally annexed by Qi in 286, with troops from Chu and Wei serving on behalf of Qi'. Cliopatria adds the land to Qi only in 284.

region.text: all of Qi but Ju and Jimo

ledger.note: 284: Yan's Yue Yi sacks Linzi and occupies Qi. 'his capital city of Linzi was invaded and sacked in 284 BC by General Yue Yi of Yan'; 'The king fled to Ju, which along with Jimo was one of the only two Qi cities that remained unoccupied'; 'All but two cities of Qi were conquered.' The Warring States page: a Zhao-led alliance attacked Qi after 284 and 'Yan would hold control over Qi until 279'; the Yue Yi page: 'except for two cities, the entire territory of Qi was brought under control'. The places of Ju and Jimo are the researcher's.

region.text: the Song land that Chu holds in Cliopatria's 247 shape (114.7-117.6 E, 34.8-36.2 N)

ledger.note: By 284: Qi loses the Song land. 'Qi was promptly attacked in its turn and lost all the territory it had gained.' The page gives no year ('promptly' after 286); 284 is the year of the Yan invasion. Cliopatria moves the land to Chu only in 247 and the Chu dossier has 'Chu's share of Song' from 286. Confidence 1.

279: Qi is restored. 'Yan would hold control over Qi until 279 BC, whereupon the state of Qi would be restored'; the King Min page: Wangsun Jia 'with Tian Dan then reconquered the seventy cities of Qi' (no year on that page).

221: Qin conquers Qi, the last of the Warring States. Infobox 'Conquered by Qin: 221 BCE'; the history text: 'The Warring States period ended with the Qin conquest of Qi, which was the last to fall, in 222' (the page's two years differ). The Qin wars of unification page (opened for the qin dossier): 'Tian Jian ... surrendered to Qin without putting up a fight'. The old Qi ends here; it is revived in 206.

206: Xiang Yu makes Tian Du King of Qi. The Eighteen Kingdoms table: 'Tian Du, Qi, western and central Shandong'; Jiaodong (Tian Fu, 'eastern Shandong') and Jibei (Tian An, 'northern Shandong') are cut from the old Qi, 'collectively known as the Three Qis'. The year is the page's 206 BCE division.

region.text: the revived Qi, 'Defeated by Liu Bang'

ledger.note: 204: the revived Qi falls to Han. The Eighteen Kingdoms table: Qi 'Defeated by Liu Bang'; Tian Rong's reunification of the three Qis ('Tian Rong conquered Jiaodong and Jibei, reuniting the old Qi state', [citation needed]) and Han Xin's invasion are undated or absent from the page; 204 is Cliopatria's last year for the row.

wars.name: Battle of An
wars.outcome: Jin defeated Qi, which had invaded Lu and Wey; no border moved.
wars.note: 'only to be defeated by Jin itself at the Battle of An in 589'; rulers table: Duke Qing 'Defeated by Jin at Battle of An'.

wars.name: Conquest of Song
wars.outcome: Qi destroyed and annexed Song, with Chu and Wei troops serving on its behalf; Qi was then attacked and lost the gains.
wars.note: Song page: 'the kingdom was finally annexed by Qi in 286, with troops from Chu and Wei serving on behalf of Qi'. The page does not say how Song was divided.

wars.name: Yan-led invasion of Qi (Battle of Jixi)

zones.text: all of Qi but Ju and Jimo

wars.outcome: The allies defeated Qi at Jixi, Yan's Yue Yi sacked Linzi in 284 and held all but two cities until Qi was restored in 279.
wars.note: 'the troops of Yan, Qin, Zhao, Han, Wei, and Chu launched the Battle of Jixi (濟西之戰) against Qi'; the page dates only the sack of Linzi (284). The Warring States page: the alliance was 'lead under the guidance the Zhao' and Yan held Qi 'until 279'.

wars.name: Qin conquest of Qi
wars.outcome: Qin conquered Qi, the last of the Warring States, ending Qi until the Eighteen Kingdoms of 206.

wars.name: Revolt of Tian Rong against the Three Qis
wars.outcome: Tian Rong rebelled against Tian Du and 'conquered Jiaodong and Jibei, reuniting the old Qi state' (Eighteen Kingdoms, [citation needed]); the page gives no year or month.
wars.note: Cliopatria keeps the Three Qis as separate shapes to 204.

certainty.note: No treaty line is dated; the frontier with Lu, Jin, Wei and Yan is approximate throughout, and the Shandong coast is the only fixed edge. The Long Wall against Yue and Chu is mentioned only on the Yue page (not opened for this).

notes: Wikidata Q1143524 is shared with 'northern-qi' (Northern Qi 555-576, a Xianbei-Chinese dynasty): a different state; this dossier covers only the Cliopatria Name 'Qi', all 11 shapes. One dossier for two Qi: the old Qi ends in 221 (loss to Qin) and the Tian Du Qi of 206-204 (Eighteen Kingdoms) is the Cliopatria row's last shape; the dossier ends in 204 with a gap 220-207 (no events there; the gain at 206 re-opens it). If the reviewer prefers, the 206-204 Qi could be a separate dossier. Jiaodong and Jibei (206-204) are Cliopatria rows of group ea-02 and are not Qi's successors; their lands come from the old Qi's shape. Needs a dossier or a page: the small states Qi annexed (Zhu 祝 768, Guo 670, Zhang 664, Yang 660, Tan 684, Sui 681, Ji 690, Lai 567, Cheng 408, Xue and Pi 418; states table, none located); Ju (state), Lai (state), Tan; Yan's Yue Yi occupation is Yan's `occupation_start` mirror (the yan dossier of group ea-01 should record it). Not on any page opened: the year of Tian Dan's recovery (279 is the Warring States page's, the King Min page has no year), Han Xin's 204 invasion of Qi, Guiling 353 and Maling 341, the Long Wall, the Qi hegemony of Duke Huan beyond '685-643' and the 667 assembly (Spring and Autumn period page: 'By 667, Qi had clearly shown its economic and military predominance'), and Qi's Jimo and Ju coordinates. The 284 correction rests on the King Min page's 'promptly' and on Cliopatria's 247 shape, a reading. Budget: 7 pages listed (5 allowed): the Song and Yue Yi pages were opened to check 286 and 284 and are cited as second pages. Region names: 'Zibo' (alias Linzi) is in the gazetteer; Yingqiu, Bogu, Ju and Jimo are not (coordinates used); gazetteer_names_needed: Yingqiu, Bogu, Ju, Jimo.
